scope: Real watchdog CLI, genuine Claude CLI processes named by disposable lock records, and actual watcher/arm processes in marked lab homes on a private 120x40 tmux socket. Beacon ages and ledger records were fault-injection data. Real command-channel notifications were persisted locally. The gate-only arm adapter clears inherited path overrides before exec of the real arm; it does not bypass lifecycle authorization or fake the stop.
setup_repairs: Used the supported short socket directory, allowed slower host command completion, waited for full watcher identity publication, and supplied an operator resume command that consumes the real wake-drain acknowledgement before re-arming. Frozen watchers were tested as failed-recovery containment, not successful recovery.

scenarios.name: Closed home with no supervision stays idle
Removed home is not recreated by the watchdog
Missing session without a resume command alarms only after repeated failure and rate-limits alerts
A running Claude CLI with bound session-lock evidence is healthy at 1000 seconds and stale at 3700 seconds even with threshold 7200
A live Claude CLI named by the session lock exposes a dead Stop-arm owner past the ordinary 900-second threshold
Relative homes and code roots render a typed launchd contract that executes correctly from the generated working directory
Live watchdog identity excludes a contender; reused-PID directory and symlink locks are reclaimed without signalling the unrelated process
A stale real watcher is stopped home-locally and restored by an operator resume command without an alarm
An unresponsive real watcher fails recovery and raises the configured alarm only after repeated attempts
Rendering and checking an isolated home do not implicitly install a login agent
scenarios.reason: The real launchctl consumer reports that the generated disposable label is not registered.

limit: No LaunchAgent installation/bootstrap, login restart, or reboot was performed; those require explicit authority to change system state outside the worktree.
